The 75% payout is presented as conservative, but because next-12m DPS is subtracted in the roll a higher, actual payout would lower the target, so the low payout is accretive. The claim that September carries more net cash than the December roll is backwards (2,991.2 vs 3,138.9).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: link1_share of 1.2% is entered as a gross COGS share and then multiplied again by (1 - 0.75 pass), giving a 0.3% net coal linkage, against the analyst own basis that the gross coal slice is roughly a quarter of the 43% fuel-and-power share (about 10.8%) and against the cement peer BLES at 12%. The deck paths themselves tie: ICI-4 62.0/52.5/46.0 and Brent 96/84.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual or guidance without a source: Q4 2026 EBITDA margin -2.4pp; payout 75% against 97-98% of clean EPS, a 15% DPS cut to 399 from 468; capex at 8.0% of revenue against the 6.3% nine-month cash-plus-lease run-rate; working capital stepped from 3.7% to 5.2% of revenue (348bn of FY2026E FCFF). The scenario shocks do mirror (volume 0.95/1.05, price 0.94/1.06, gross margin -/+2.5pp, capex 1.25/0.8), which is a real improvement on the prior draft.

calibration.note: cov_engine qc returns no blocking flags, no drift flags and no orphan justifications. The calibration gap is -0.88pp (FY2026E EBITDA margin 19.43% vs FY2025A restated 20.30%), inside the gate; the direction is explained by the unrebased FY2026E margin above, not by a data error.

signoff.notes: APPROVED, with the eight QC FIX items carried as conditions for the next update rather than publication blockers, because none of them moves the rating and every one of them, if corrected, moves the target UP. Checks run and their outcome. (1) Most likely, not most cautious. The base case is anchored on the last actual: FY2026E revenue of 19,378.1bn is 9M actual 14,070.8bn plus one Q4 at the 9M margin 20.1% on Q4 volume of about 6.0 Mt, which is 9M2025's Q4 5.50 Mt times the 9M growth rate of +9.0% [S4 F10, F36], and realised price of 893k/t is the 9M print of 893.5 [S4 F12]; gross margin 33.7 pre-link against 32.0 reported 9M; capex 8.0% of revenue sits between the FY2025 cash capex 5.7% and the accrual 10.0% on a reconciled basis [S2 F5, S3 F42]; tax 19.5% is above the FY2025A 17.8% and below the 9M 19.9%; payout 90% pays DPS 511 against the 468 actually paid, so no unsourced dividend cut remains [S3 F26]. Both scenario wings shock the same four drivers, mirrored, so there is no asymmetric bear. The deck link is house law and is a tailwind the company must be graded on: ICI-4 62.0 in FY2026E falling to 46.0 long run against a spot of 65.06, and Brent 84.0 against a spot of 92.4 - a falling cost deck, not conservatism. The residual direction of error is conservative: Q5 (legs struck on FY2025A 3,599.8, not the LTM 3,959.9 the text claims) is worth about +88 of target at the 0.25 weight, and Q11 (P/BV 0.327x against a justified 0.558x, and against a cement-only peer median of about 0.43x) about +60; correcting both would print a target near 7,360, not a lower one. The bear at 5,583 is essentially the 5,600 price, so the 38.0% total return does not depend on the downside being understated; the target of 7,215 is 5.3x FY2026E EBITDA and 1.04x September book, against a DCF that prints 6.3x, which is the right shape for a net-cash market leader in a trough. (2) Classification and method card fit. CEMENT sits under BASIC_MATERIALS in the desk coverage, and VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL is the right card: a price-taking commodity with a capacity cycle, a long-lived asset DCF at 60%, volume times price revenue at 0.001, and the two industry cost links (ICI-4 for kiln fuel, Brent for quarry and distribution diesel). The template cannot carry an FX driver and the report says so in section 5 rather than pretending otherwise. (3) Evidence law. Facts PASS and lint PASS on check. Every printed model number reproduces: the 6,971 blend is 0.60 x 8,436 + 0.25 x 6,275 + 0.15 x 2,273, the 7,322 base is 6,971 x 1.1236 less 511, and 7,215 is the 50/30/20 scenario weight. The restatement of D&A to the LK total 1,562.9 is keyed to facts and not modelled around [S2 F3]. Section 4 no longer presents the cross-checks as a screen; the peer-median override is stated with its value effect, which is the C5 fix holding. (4) Batch bias. CEMENT is not one-sided - BLES BUY, CMNT SELL - so there is no shared-input tilt to look for. INTP's 11.9% WACC is the same sector build as its peers, and the multiple legs pull the target below the DCF, which is a downward not an upward tilt. Conditions to clear in the next version; all eight are known-false text or mechanics in a document that publishes, all under 1.5% of target individually, and none of them justifies re-opening the call. Q1 section 5 prints the treasury block as 599.0% of the shares - the pct filter doubles F59 5.99; the true figure is 5.99% and F45 and S2 p.12 say so. Q2 the section 4 EV walk prints EV 24,709.0 from cash less loans less leases alone, which walks to 25,545, not 24,709; the +837.1 investment in associates is in the engine and must be printed in the walk [S3 p.4]. Q3 valuation.weights_basis in fund record still carries the pre-revision arithmetic - DCF 7,786, blend 6,581, drag 1,205 - against the engine's 8,436 / 6,971 / 1,465. Q4 the cost-of-capital paragraph omits the 1.62pp sovereign default spread the engine subtracts, so its own build adds to 14.0%, not the 12.4% it prints; state 7.45 - 1.62 + 0.9764 x (4.23 + 2.46) = 12.36%. Q5 section 4 and the C2 rebuttal both say the engine strikes the multiple legs on trailing LTM; it strikes them on FY2025A EBITDA 3,599.8 (LTM would be 3,959.9). The C2 conclusion still stands - a mid-cycle multiple on trough earnings is the error to avoid - but the sentence describing the engine is false and the trough denominator is itself a conservative choice that should be disclosed as such. Q6 show the link1_share 10.8% bridge: fuel and power 4,948.3 is 41.4% of FY2025 cost of revenues [S2 F57] and coal is roughly a quarter of it after the 33.6% alternative-fuel rate. Q7 link1_pass 0.75 has no source and its own basis argues the opposite (the 9M price effect of -11bn says prices did not carry the fuel move); source the contract or surcharge, or set it consistently and disclose the net coal sensitivity of about 3% of cost of revenues. Q8 valuation.post_bs_review asserts no rights issue, divestment, acquisition or special dividend on S6 (demand commentary) and S7 (price war), neither of which can carry a negative existence claim; cite the news-pack search actually run - S8 is 12 Nov 2026 - or state that the check was limited to the pack. Notes, not conditions: Q10 opex drifting 21.0% to 20.6% by FY2030E is unsourced but worth under 1% of the DCF; Q9 section 2 should say the rupiah path is context and not a modelled driver; the note is 7,205 words against a 500-3,500 house range for a results update and should be cut to the table-supported core at the next update. I would also widen the P/BV leg toward the cement-only peer median (about 0.43x) rather than the mixed peer set's 0.327x when the file is next opened, since the most-likely standard cuts both ways and this leg is the one place the file sits below it.

bias.note: Base anchors on the last actual and its prices: FY2026E volume 21.700 Mt vs 19.941 Mt FY2025A on the 9M 15.747 Mt actual (+9.0%), realised price 893,000 vs 889,000 (flat), gross margin 32.3% vs 32.5%, opex 21.0% vs 21.1% and EBITDA margin 20.1% vs 20.3%, so the year earns what the company printed rather than a haircut or a stretch (S2, S4 p.11). Departures are sourced: FY2027E-FY2030E volume +3.2/+3.1/+3.0/+2.9% on the house deck 3.3% 2025-28 demand CAGR (S4 p.5); price +0.8% then +2.0% a year, a ~1% real decline argued from four years of flat ASP and the director calling the price war unavoidable (S7). Two documented conservatisms - the P/BV leg at the 0.327 peer median against a 0.556 justified multiple, and both multiple legs on FY2025A EBITDA nine months stale - are offset by one unsourced optimism, opex drifting 21.0% to 20.6%. Scenarios mirror the same four drivers (volume 0.95/1.05, price 0.94/1.06, gross margin -2/+2pp, opex +2/-2pp) at 50/30/20. Net neutral, and TR 38.0% is below the 40% extreme-call trigger; the prose does not overstate it.

findings.finding: Section 5 renders the treasury block as 210.4924 m shares and 599.0% of the shares. Fact F59 is 5.99 (percent) and the pct filter multiplies by 100, so the printed number is 100x the truth and contradicts F45 and S2 p.12 (5.99% of the count).

Section 4 states the capitalisation is cash 4,738.6 less bank loans 2,000.0 less leases 584.4 and prints EV 24,709.0 and Rp8,436. That walk omits the +837.1 of investment in associates in the engine DCF (S3 p.4, Investasi pada entitas asosiasi 837.098), so a reader recomputing from the prose gets equity 26,863.1 and Rp8,181, a 3.0% (Rp255/share) gap.

valuation.weights_basis still says the DCF values the shares at 7,786 and the three methods average 6,581 with the cross-checks dragging the DCF down by about 1,205, while the engine prints DCF 8,436, blend 6,971 and a drag of 1,465. Section 4 sends the reader to that block to check the weights.

The cost-of-capital paragraph omits the sovereign default spread the engine subtracts: COE = rf 7.45% - default spread 1.62% + 0.9764 x (ERP 4.23% + CRP 2.46%) = 12.36%. As written (7.4 + 0.98 x 4.2 + 2.5) the reader gets 14.0%, not 12.4%.

Both multiple legs are described as struck on trailing last-twelve-month earnings (section 4 and the C2 rebuttal), but the engine strikes them on FY2025A EBITDA of 3,599.8. The LTM to 30 Sep 2026 is 3,959.9 (3,599.8 - 9M2025 2,464.5 + 9M2026 2,824.6), 10.0% higher; at 4.89x that is about Rp536 on the leg and Rp150 on the target, in the conservative direction.

link1_share 10.8% is a key input whose derivation is not shown. S4 p.12 puts fuel and power at 43% of cost of revenues and the alternative-fuel rate at 33.6%, so 10.8% of COGS implies coal is only about a quarter of the fuel-and-power line; a literal read gives 15-20%. The value effect of the whole 10.8-20% range is only about Rp100-150 of target because the deck ICI-4 path is near flat after FY2027E, so this is a FIX, not a BLOCK.

link1_pass 0.75 has no supporting source and its own justification argues the opposite: it cites the 9M price effect of -11bn (cement prices did not carry the fuel move) and the company absorbing the fuel move in its cost base, which implies a low pass-through, not 75%.

valuation.post_bs_review says no rights issue, divestment, acquisition or special dividend has been announced, cited to S6 (a demand commentary) and S7 (a price-war piece). Neither can evidence the absence of a corporate action, and the news pack holds one item (S8, 12 Nov 2026).

Section 2 says the external influences carried are the coal deck, Brent, the rupiah and Indonesian rates and prints an FX path, but drivers_used holds only coal and Brent, and section 5 correctly says the template has no rupiah driver. No FX enters the model.
opex_pct drifts 21.0% to 20.6% by FY2030E on unsourced volume leverage, worth about Rp90-95bn of FY2030E EBITDA, under 1% of the DCF value.

The P/BV leg at 0.327x carries 15% of the weight and sits far below the 0.556x the own-model (ROE 8.0% - g 2.5%) / (COE 12.4% - g 2.5%) justifies. The override is documented and the red team rebuttal stands, so this is advice, not a defect; the anchor is worth roughly Rp230-270 of target on the most-likely standard.
